_meta.source: Written for this app. Stage structure follows the actual shape of the Singapore education and training system; choices are written so that none is the correct answer.
_meta.notes: No choice in this file is scored as right or wrong, and no combination of choices produces a failure. Every stage advances. The ledger records what a player accumulated, not how well they did. Doors never go to zero: the engine asserts this and the dev sweep checks it.

stages.title: Sec 3
stages.situation: New subjects, new classes, and for the first time some of your friends are in different rooms from you. The year is longer than it looks.

choices.label: Go hard at the subjects you are already good at
choices.outcome: You get noticeably better at the things you were already decent at. It feels good and it is a narrower year than it could have been.

choices.label: Put real effort into the subject you find hardest
choices.outcome: It is a slog. By the end of the year you are still not top of the class and you are no longer afraid of it, which turns out to matter more.

choices.label: Join something outside the classroom and take it seriously
choices.outcome: It costs you time you would have spent studying. You end the year knowing three adults who would vouch for you.

stages.title: Sec 4
stages.situation: The exam year. Everyone around you has an opinion about what you should do next, and most of them have only ever seen one route.

choices.label: Focus entirely on the results
choices.outcome: A clean, narrow year. You go into the exams as ready as you were going to be.

choices.label: Study, and also go and look at what is actually out there
choices.outcome: You lose a few weekends to open houses. You now know about four courses you had never heard of, one of which you cannot stop thinking about.

choices.label: Apply through the Early Admissions Exercise
choices.outcome: You have to write down what you want and say it to a stranger. Whatever the outcome, you have now said it out loud once.

stages.title: Results
stages.situation: The envelope. Whatever is in it, this is the moment that feels like a verdict and is not one.

choices.label: Take the route your results point at most directly
choices.outcome: Straightforward, and there is nothing wrong with straightforward. You start in September.

choices.label: Take a longer route toward something you actually want
choices.outcome: It will take you a year or two more than your friends. You have chosen the destination rather than the shortest available road.

choices.label: Take a fifth year to widen what is available
choices.outcome: One more year in the same uniform. Some of your friends do not understand it. In ten years nobody can tell.

stages.title: First year after secondary
stages.situation: Nobody is checking whether you did the reading. The course is harder than school in a different way, and the people are from everywhere.

choices.label: Keep your head down and do the work
choices.outcome: Solid marks, few surprises. You are on track.

choices.label: Get involved in something beyond the course
choices.outcome: Your marks dip slightly. You now know people two years ahead of you who tell you things the handbook does not.

choices.label: Start something of your own on the side
choices.outcome: Most of your weekends go. You have something to show that is entirely yours.

stages.title: Finishing
stages.situation: The end is visible. The choice now is what you do with the qualification you are about to hold.

choices.label: Go straight into work
choices.outcome: You are earning while others are still studying. The learning continues, it just happens on someone's payroll.

choices.label: Keep studying, further up
choices.outcome: More years, more debt of time, a wider set of roles at the end of it.

choices.label: Take a work study route and do both
choices.outcome: Employed and studying at once. It is genuinely hard and you finish with both.

stages.title: Early working years
stages.situation: You are in it now. The work is not what the course described, and nobody warned you how much of a job is other people.

choices.label: Get very good at the specific thing you were hired for
choices.outcome: You become the person they come to for that. Deep and narrow.

choices.label: Learn how the whole place works, not just your part
choices.outcome: You are not the best at any one task and you can see how the pieces fit, which is rarer.

choices.label: Keep building the thing on the side
choices.outcome: Two lives at once, tiring and interesting. The side thing is starting to be known.

stages.title: The first real crossroads
stages.situation: You could stay on this road for another decade and it would be fine. Something in you is asking whether fine is the plan.

choices.label: Stay and go deeper
choices.outcome: Mastery is a real thing and it takes years. You are choosing to spend them.

choices.label: Move sideways into an adjacent field
choices.outcome: Most of what you know still applies. You are a beginner again in the parts that do not, which is uncomfortable and short lived.

choices.label: Upgrade formally, part time, while working
choices.outcome: Two years of evenings. A qualification you did not have at nineteen.

stages.title: Building something
stages.situation: You have enough experience now that people ask your opinion. That is a kind of power and it is easy to spend badly.

choices.label: Take responsibility for other people's work
choices.outcome: Managing is a different job than doing, and you have to learn it from scratch.

choices.label: Stay hands on and become genuinely expert
choices.outcome: You keep doing the work rather than talking about it. Fewer meetings, more craft.

choices.label: Start your own thing
choices.outcome: Everything now depends on you, which is the terrifying part and the point.

stages.title: The ground moves
stages.situation: Your field is not what it was when you entered it. Some of what you were paid for is now done differently, or by something else.

choices.label: Learn the new tools early
choices.outcome: You are ahead of the curve rather than under it. The change becomes an advantage.

choices.label: Move to the part of the field this did not touch
choices.outcome: A sensible sidestep. The work is still there and it is quieter.

choices.label: Retrain properly, into something else
choices.outcome: You use what the system provides for this and you start again on purpose. It is not a fall. It is a decision.

stages.title: Looking back and forward
stages.situation: You are perhaps halfway through your working life. There is a lot of it left.

choices.label: Use the mid career support and do the thing you always meant to
choices.outcome: A $4,000 credit, an allowance while you study, and up to 90 percent off a full time diploma. You are the oldest in the room and it does not matter.

choices.label: Teach what you know to people coming up
choices.outcome: You tell them the real version, including the parts that went badly. It is more useful to them than the tidy one.

choices.label: Keep going, and keep learning inside the work
choices.outcome: No dramatic move. Steady, deliberate, and still curious, which is rarer at forty two than it sounds.

endingFrames.title: You kept the map wide open.
endingFrames.body: You ended up with more available to you than you started with. That is not luck. It is what happens when someone keeps looking.

endingFrames.title: You got genuinely good at something.
endingFrames.body: Depth is its own kind of freedom. People who are properly skilled at a thing are rarely short of options.

endingFrames.title: People know who you are.
endingFrames.body: Most of what happens to people at work comes through someone who thought of them. You gave a lot of people the chance to think of you.

endingFrames.title: You made things.
endingFrames.body: There is a record of what you can do that does not depend on anyone's grading. That record opened doors that no aggregate could have.
